summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2026 is dominated by the major cloud providers—AWS, Microsoft, and Google—who offer managed access to foundation models within a customer's existing cloud security perimeter, so prompts and data never leave the governed environment. There is no single winner; the best fit depends on an organization's existing cloud contracts, data residency requirements, and model preferences. A second tier of data-platform and governance-focused vendors (Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx, Oracle, Cloudflare) competes by bringing AI to where enterprise data already lives.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: inference runs inside the enterprise's own cloud VPC/tenant so sensitive prompts and outputs never leave the governed boundary or train the model vendor's systems.
Compliance and governance: built-in audit logging, access controls, and certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, GDPR) that direct vendor APIs often do not provide at enterprise scale.
Single billing and consolidated procurement: AI spend rolls into existing cloud commitments (EDP/MACC/committed-use discounts) rather than requiring new vendor contracts and payment relationships.

Model choice and avoiding lock-in: one secure API gives access to many foundation models (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, GPT, etc.), letting teams swap or route between models without re-architecting integrations.
Integration with existing infrastructure: native connection to the enterprise's data lakes, IAM, networking, monitoring, and MLOps tooling already deployed in that cloud.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service (Azure AI Foundry)
available_models: models via Azure AI Foundry Model Catalog
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens (input/output) plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; billed through Azure with MACC commitments.
key_features: Deep integration with Microsoft 365 and Copilot stack
platforms.best_for: Enterprises standardized on Microsoft/Azure that want first-party access to the latest OpenAI (GPT/o-series) models with strong governance.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing, Batch (discounted), and Provisioned Throughput (reserved model units per hour/month); billed through AWS with EDP discounts.
platforms.best_for: AWS-centric enterprises wanting the broadest multi-model choice (especially Anthropic Claude) with no vendor lock-in and strong serverless integration.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI (Model Garden)
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per-token (per character/image) plus Provisioned Throughput measured in GSUs (e.g., 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec sustained); committed-use discounts via Google Cloud.
key_features: VPC Service Controls / Private Service Connect
Grounding with Google Search and enterprise data
platforms.best_for: Data/ML-heavy enterprises on Google Cloud wanting first-party Gemini models plus a large multi-vendor Model Garden and strong data-platform integration.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits (per-token/per-function), billed through the existing Snowflake contract.
key_features: AI runs inside the Snowflake data perimeter (no data movement)
platforms.best_for: Organizations with data already governed in Snowflake wanting to run LLM inference and RAG directly against that data without exporting it.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Subscription plus consumption (Resource Units / per-token); available on IBM Cloud, on-premises, and hybrid via Cloud Pak for Data / Red Hat OpenShift.
key_features: watsonx.governance (AI assurance, lifecycle monitoring, risk controls)
Named a Leader in 2026 Gartner MQ for AI Platforms
platforms.best_for: Highly regulated enterprises (banking, government, healthcare) needing on-prem/hybrid deployment plus deep AI governance and assurance.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-character/token on-demand plus Dedicated AI Clusters (reserved GPU capacity) billed through OCI; strong Universal Credits commitments.
key_features: Dedicated AI Clusters for isolated capacity
EU Sovereign Cloud and dedicated regions
platforms.best_for: Oracle database and ERP/Fusion customers wanting managed GenAI close to their Oracle data and committed OCI spend.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
available_models: open models via AI Gateway to OpenAI/Anthropic
platforms.pricing: Usage-based per neuron/token on Cloudflare's global edge network; generous free tier, pay-as-you-go beyond.
key_features: Serverless inference at the global edge (low latency)
AI Gateway for caching, rate-limiting, and observability across providers
Vectorize vector DB and R2 integration
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, globally distributed inference and a unified gateway/observability layer in front of multiple model providers.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI (Foundation Model APIs)
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs / pay-per-token) within the Databricks lakehouse; committed-use discounts.
key_features: Model Serving within the lakehouse perimeter
Mosaic AI Gateway and AI/BI Genie
platforms.best_for: Data engineering and ML teams on the Databricks lakehouse wanting unified governance across data, custom models, and foundation-model inference.
